entities.name: GlmU
observations: The 455-residue query protein is a bifunctional bacterial GlmU homolog; curated references show 44.2–47.4% identity over 93.0–94.1% sequence coverage with E-values of 7.18e-120 to 1.19e-117.

The N-terminal region (approximately residues 1–230) is a UDP-GlcNAc pyrophosphorylase domain, followed by a linker and a C-terminal glucosamine-1-phosphate N-acetyltransferase domain (approximately residues 252–455).
The enzyme catalyzes the final two steps of UDP-N-acetylglucosamine biosynthesis and is reported as cytosolic, homotrimeric, and Mg2+-binding in curated homologs.
Sequence-derived properties: 455 residues, approximately 49.5 kDa, theoretical pI 5.80.

source_tools.relevance: Sequence analysis, Pfam domains, and curated Swiss-Prot homolog evidence

observations: Glucosamine-1-phosphate + acetyl-CoA -> N-acetylglucosamine-1-phosphate + CoA + H+, Rhea RHEA:13725; assigned to the C-terminal GlmU acetyltransferase domain.

entities.name: UDP-GlcNAc formation
observations: N-acetylglucosamine-1-phosphate + UTP + H+ -> UDP-N-acetylglucosamine + diphosphate, Rhea RHEA:13509; assigned to the N-terminal GlmU pyrophosphorylase domain.
The reaction uses Mg2+ according to curated GlmU homolog annotations.

entities.name: UDP-GlcNAc biosynthesis
observations: GlmU performs the final two sequential reactions in de novo UDP-N-acetylglucosamine biosynthesis, supporting peptidoglycan and, where applicable, lipid A production.
